agents.name: Lorlatinib
agents.explanation: Lorlatinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that helps some lung cancers grow. It can reach the brain, an important site of disease in ALK-positive lung cancer. It is selected using an ALK test. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.

agents.watch: Report thinking, mood, speech, breathing or heart symptoms promptly and attend lipid, glucose and other monitoring.
risks: Raised cholesterol and triglycerides; pancreatic inflammation may occur

questions.q: Why is an ALK test needed?
questions.a: Lorlatinib is intended for cancers with a specific ALK change. Your team checks the result and whether the treatment fits your previous medicines.

questions.q: How long will I take it?
questions.a: Lorlatinib is taken once daily continuously, with no planned rest week. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of treatment cycles.

questions.q: What if I miss a dose or vomit?
questions.a: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered if the next dose is at least four hours away; otherwise skip it. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, do not take another tablet; take the next dose at the usual time. These instructions follow the current product leaflet.

questions.q: Why are cholesterol tests needed if I feel well?
questions.a: Blood fats can rise without symptoms. Regular tests let the team treat this early. Raised cholesterol does not always mean lorlatinib must stop; your clinician uses the actual results and your overall condition.

questions.q: What changes should my family or friends notice?
questions.a: Changes in memory, concentration, mood, speech, behaviour or perceptions should be reported promptly. Agree with the team and someone you trust how changes will be noticed, if helpful.
Lorlatinib can affect thinking and other CNS functions. Use caution and discuss driving or operating machinery, particularly if symptoms occur.

questions.q: Does a dose reduction mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. A hold or reduction may allow side effects to recover and reduce harm. The team reviews cancer control separately and explains the restart plan.

questions.q: What belongs in the consent discussion?
questions.a: Discuss your aim, expected benefits and uncertainty, reasonable alternatives including not proceeding, serious and lasting risks, daily practicalities, contraception, fertility, support needs and your right to reconsider.

support.title: Cholesterol and other medicines

support.title: Sickness and daily wellbeing
support.text: This oral regimen has minimal to low sickness risk. Use anti-sickness medicine only according to your own plan and report persistent vomiting or poor intake. A standard chemotherapy steroid or anti-sickness course is not automatically needed.

support.title: Thinking, mood and practical support
support.text: Ask someone you trust to help notice changes in thinking, mood, speech or behaviour, if you wish. Report changes early. Lorlatinib can affect driving and machine use, especially when CNS effects are present; discuss whether it is safe for you.

support.title: Pregnancy, fertility and feeding
support.text: Lorlatinib may harm an unborn baby and make hormonal contraception less effective. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 35 days afterwards; discuss any unavoidable hormonal method and barrier protection. Men with partners who could become pregnant need effective contraception including a condom during treatment and for at least 14 weeks afterwards; condoms are also needed with a pregnant partner. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree when it can safely resume with the team.

evidence.title: Evidence differs before and after earlier ALK treatment
evidence.intro: A first-line randomised trial and separate later-line cohorts answer different questions.
evidence.population: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC; untreated patients in CROWN and previously treated patients in the global phase 2 study.
evidence.comparison_label: Crizotinib in CROWN; no comparator in phase 2
evidence.interpretation: The first-line CROWN trial found longer control of cancer and brain progression with lorlatinib than with crizotinib. Separate studies showed activity after earlier ALK medicines. Outcomes depend on the treatment setting and cannot predict one person’s benefit; the treatments have different monitoring and side-effect burdens.
evidence.limitations: First-line and later-line results are not interchangeable. Current evidence does not provide a personal prognosis or a direct comparison against every other ALK treatment.

clinical.component_rationale: Lorlatinib blocks the abnormal ALK protein that helps some lung cancers grow. It can reach the brain, an important site of disease in ALK-positive lung cancer. It is selected using an ALK test. It can also affect healthy tissues, so blood tests and symptom checks remain important.
key_points: Fresh NCCP 00570 v3 lists only 00570a; first-line EMA licence is separate and source-verification gated.
Continuous 100 mg once daily; source reduction levels 75 mg then 50 mg, with discontinuation if 50 mg not tolerated.
Severe lipid ranges continue at the same dose with lipid therapy; life-threatening levels require a hold. Do not treat all grade 3 cholesterol as a stop.
Grade 2–3 CNS toxicity holds until≤1 then reduced; grade 4 permanently stops.
Confirmed ILDgrade 1–2 holds to baseline, then reduced; grade ≥3, recurrence or failure after 6 weeks of hold plus steroids permanently stops.
AV-block actions use grade and symptoms, not an imported QTc threshold; complete block restart requires specialist pacing/PR assessment.
Current EMA hepatic guidance conflicts with NCCP: no automatic hepatic dose. Renal and interaction reductions must not be multiplied.

rationale.summary: Lorlatinib aims to control ALK-positive advanced lung cancer, including disease in the brain where present. Your oncology team explains the likely benefit, treatment line and alternatives for your situation. This guide covers lorlatinib alone for ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. The available Irish NCCP v3 document lists use after particular earlier ALK medicines. The current European licence also includes people who have not had an ALK inhibitor. rationale.setting: ALK-positive advanced NSCLC · specified later-line NCCP indication; separate licensed first-line context
rationale.line: NCCP 00570a after specified ALK therapy; EMA first-line licence discussed separately with source verification.
factors: ALK result, exact previous therapy/progression, brain disease, performance status and organ function.
CNS/psychiatric function, cardiac conduction, lipids, glucose, BP, interactions and patient priorities.
alternatives: Discuss current MDT-selected ALK therapies, trials, other systemic options and supportive care including not proceeding; no cross-trial ranking is made.
limitations: CROWN compared first-line lorlatinib with crizotinib, not other contemporary ALK inhibitors. Its 2026 seven-year update is a post hoc investigator-assessed analysis; formal between-arm testing was not performed and protocol-specified overall survival analysis remains immature.
Seven-year PFS is not seven-year overall survival. The conditional 79% figure applies only to participants event-free at 24 months, so it is omitted from the main benefit display.

The 2018 phase 2 study was single-arm and included differing prior ALK treatments. The pooled 47% response includes crizotinib-only patients and must not be assigned to the narrower NCCP 00570a population.

Fresh NCCP v3 has only 00570a. Indexed v4/00570b could not be downloaded; EMA licence, NCCP indication and reimbursement are distinct. First-line use requires current local source/access verification.
Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI approval remains pending.

evidence.comparison: Lorlatinib 100 mg once daily versus crizotinib 250 mg twice daily in CROWN; no randomised comparator in phase 2.

endpoints.metric: CROWN 2026: investigator-assessed seven-year PFS from randomisation
endpoints.interpretation: Data cutoff 31 October 2025; median follow-up 83.0 versus 77.2 months. Median PFS not reached (95% CI 68.5–NR) versus 9.1 months (7.4–10.9). Post hoc investigator assessment, no formal statistical testing; this endpoint is not overall survival.
endpoints.analysis_status: Published post hoc 7-year analysis; OS follow-up ongoing

sources.label: Shaw et al., Annals of Oncology 2026
CROWN2026 primary ASCO abstract: data cutoff and post hoc methods

endpoints.metric: Phase 2: one prior non-crizotinib ALK inhibitor (EXP3B)
endpoints.interpretation: 2018 primary analysis: 95% CI 15.9–52.4. Prior-ALK cohort, not CROWN; check exact previous therapy against NCCP 00570a.

endpoints.metric: Phase 2: two or more previous ALK inhibitors (EXP4–5)
endpoints.interpretation: 2018 primary analysis: 95% CI 29.6–48.5. Prior treatments vary; cohort is not identical to every eligible 00570a sequence. No survival advantage or comparative effect is inferred.

limitations: CROWN compared first-line lorlatinib with crizotinib, not other contemporary ALK inhibitors. Its 2026 seven-year update is a post hoc investigator-assessed analysis; formal between-arm testing was not performed and protocol-specified overall survival analysis remains immature.
Seven-year PFS is not seven-year overall survival. The conditional 79% figure applies only to participants event-free at 24 months, so it is omitted from the main benefit display.

The 2018 phase 2 study was single-arm and included differing prior ALK treatments. The pooled 47% response includes crizotinib-only patients and must not be assigned to the narrower NCCP 00570a population.

Fresh NCCP v3 has only 00570a. Indexed v4/00570b could not be downloaded; EMA licence, NCCP indication and reimbursement are distinct. First-line use requires current local source/access verification.
Independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI approval remains pending.
evidence.harms: CNS/psychiatric effects, raised lipids, hypertension, hyperglycaemia, nerve symptoms, swelling and cardiac conduction effects require active monitoring. ILD and pancreatitis can be serious. Prolonged exposure and trial-population differences limit simple toxicity comparisons; no borrowed frequency estimates are applied.

Lorlatinib is taken once daily continuously, with no planned rest week. Treatment continues while it is helping and side effects remain acceptable; there is no fixed number of treatment cycles.
Baseline and ongoing LVEF monitoring is conditional on cardiac risk or symptoms; no universal 3-month schedule is imported.

selector.label: Lorlatinib · ALK-positive advanced NSCLC
selector.scope_note: This guide covers lorlatinib alone for ALK-positive advanced non-small-cell lung cancer. The available Irish NCCP v3 document lists use after particular earlier ALK medicines. The current European licence also includes people who have not had an ALK inhibitor. The team must confirm your treatment setting and the current Irish protocol and access arrangements before prescribing; the source versions currently disagree.

support_plans.label: Continuous lorlatinib · individual supportive care
additional_support: NCCP rates this oral regimen minimal to low emetogenic risk; follow local oral-SACT prevention/rescue policy. NCIS V8 describes parenteral antiemetics and is not copied as a daily oral schedule.
No routine premedications are required. Lipid-lowering, BP/glucose and symptom treatment are individual prescriptions reviewed for interactions.

If a dose is missed, take it when remembered if the next dose is at least four hours away; otherwise skip it. Do not take two doses together. If you vomit after a dose, do not take another tablet; take the next dose at the usual time. These instructions follow the current product leaflet.

Lorlatinib may harm an unborn baby and make hormonal contraception less effective. Women who could become pregnant need highly effective non-hormonal contraception during treatment and for at least 35 days afterwards; discuss any unavoidable hormonal method and barrier protection. Men with partners who could become pregnant need effective contraception including a condom during treatment and for at least 14 weeks afterwards; condoms are also needed with a pregnant partner. Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Do not breastfeed during treatment; agree when it can safely resume with the team.
No routine G-CSF, antimicrobial prophylaxis or steroid course is specified in NCCP 00570.
